title: Marshall Hall's theorem through finite cores
abstract: Formalizes Marshall Hall's finite-index free-factor theorem for finitely generated subgroups of finite-rank free groups. The proof extracts the finitely many suffix states of a subgroup generating set, completes the resulting partial generator actions to permutations of a finite state set, identifies the connected orbit with a finite core, and extends a geodesic spanning tree to obtain an inclusion-compatible free-product decomposition. It also exposes an explicit finite permutation separator for every finitely generated subgroup and element outside it, yielding the LERF consequence. The repository also proves binary and finite-indexed free-group instances of Grushko--Neumann rank additivity, and the arbitrary-factor binary theorem. The arbitrary-factor proof is carried by a finite labelled-graph fold, source-unfold, and monochromatic-vertex contraction reduction.
authors: Ruy J. G. B. de Queiroz

informal.MarshallHall.marshallHall: Every finitely generated subgroup of a finite-rank free group is an inclusion-compatible free factor of a finite-index subgroup.
informal.LERFChallenge.freeGroup_finite_permutati: Every element outside a finitely generated subgroup of a finite-rank free group can be separated by an explicit finite permutation action.
informal.MarshallHall.rank_freeProduct_eq_add: The rank of a free product of finitely generated groups is the sum of their ranks.
